review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

3:1.sourceText: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Σάρδεσιν ἐκκλησίας γράψον Τάδε λέγει ὁ ἔχων τὰ ἑπτὰ Πνεύματα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀστέρας Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα, ὅτι ὄνομα ἔχεις ὅτι ζῇς, καὶ νεκρὸς εἶ.
3:1.targetText: “To the angel of the church in Sardis write:  These are the words of the One who holds the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars.  I know your deeds; you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead.

groups.note: The dative ἀγγέλῳ ("to the angel") supplies To.
Τάδε ("these things") introduces the words that follow.
λέγει ("says") is rendered as the noun phrase the words of.
ὄνομα ("name") is used for reputation.
ὅτι ζῇς ("that you live") is rendered for being alive.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links this letter to the previous one and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders this explanatory ὅτι ("that") with a semicolon.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the formula These are the words of; the Greek has none.

3:2.sourceText: γίνου γρηγορῶν, καὶ στήρισον τὰ λοιπὰ ἃ ἔμελλον ἀποθανεῖν· οὐ γὰρ εὕρηκά σου ἔργα πεπληρωμένα ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ μου·
3:2.targetText: Wake up and strengthen what remains, which was about to die; for I have found your deeds incomplete in the sight of My God.

groups.note: γίνου γρηγορῶν ("become watchful") is rendered Wake up.
τὰ λοιπά ("the remaining things") is rendered what remains.
οὐ … πεπληρωμένα ("not completed") is rendered incomplete.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:3.sourceText: μνημόνευε οὖν πῶς εἴληφας καὶ ἤκουσας, καὶ τήρει καὶ μετανόησον. ἐὰν οὖν μὴ γρηγορήσῃς, ἥξω ὡς κλέπτης, καὶ οὐ μὴ γνῷς ποίαν ὥραν ἥξω ἐπὶ σέ.
3:3.targetText: Remember, then, what you have received and heard. Keep it and repent. If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know the hour when I will come upon you.

groups.note: πῶς ("how") is rendered what.
οὐ μή is a strong negative, rendered not with will know.
ποίαν ὥραν ("what hour") is rendered the hour when.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here, so this καί is not separately expressed.
BSB leaves this second οὖν ("then") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of Keep; the Greek has none.

3:4.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἔχεις ὀλίγα ὀνόματα ἐν Σάρδεσιν ἃ οὐκ ἐμόλυναν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν, καὶ περιπατήσουσιν μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐν λευκοῖς, ὅτι ἄξιοί εἰσιν.
3:4.targetText: But you do have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments, and because they are worthy, they will walk with Me in white.

groups.note: ὀνόματα ("names") is used for persons.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:5.sourceText: Ὁ νικῶν οὕτως περιβαλεῖται ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐξαλείψω τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῆς βίβλου τῆς ζωῆς, καὶ ὁμολογήσω τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Πατρός μου καὶ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ.
3:5.targetText: Like them, he who overcomes will be dressed in white. And I will never blot out his name from the Book of Life, but I will confess his name before My Father and His angels.

groups.note: οὕτως ("in this way") is rendered Like them, pointing back to the worthy ones of verse 4.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς ("in white garments") as in white, without a word for garments.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not repeat before with His angels.

3:6.sourceText: Ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ Πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.
3:6.targetText: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

3:7.sourceText: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Φιλαδελφίᾳ ἐκκλησίας γράψον Τάδε λέγει ὁ ἅγιος, ὁ ἀληθινός, ὁ ἔχων τὴν κλεῖν Δαυείδ, ὁ ἀνοίγων καὶ οὐδεὶς κλείσει, καὶ κλείων καὶ οὐδεὶς ἀνοίγει
3:7.targetText: To the angel of the church in Philadelphia write:  These are the words of the One who is holy and true, who holds the key of David. What He opens no one can shut, and what He shuts no one can open.

groups.note: The dative ἀγγέλῳ ("to the angel") supplies To.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
Τάδε ("these things") introduces the words that follow.
λέγει ("says") is rendered as the noun phrase the words of.
The articular adjective ὁ ἅγιος ("the holy one") is rendered the One who is holy.
The article repeated with ἀληθινός ("the true one") is not separately expressed.
The article with the participle ἀνοίγων ("the one who opens") is rendered He opens.
The future κλείσει ("will shut") is rendered can shut.
κλείων ("shutting") shares the article of ὁ ἀνοίγων and is rendered as a finite verb.
The present ἀνοίγει ("opens") is rendered can open.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links this letter to the previous one and is not separately expressed.
BSB turns the following clause into the main clause, so this καί is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the formula These are the words of; the Greek has none.
English supplies a copula with holy; the Greek has none.
English joins the two titles with and; the Greek repeats the article instead.
English supplies the object of opens and shut; the Greek has none.
English supplies the object of shuts and open; the Greek has none.
English supplies He as the subject of shuts; κλείων is a participle with no person.

3:8.sourceText: Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα· ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ἐνώπιόν σου θύραν ἠνεῳγμένην, ἣν οὐδεὶς δύναται κλεῖσαι αὐτήν· ὅτι μικρὰν ἔχεις δύναμιν, καὶ ἐτήρησάς μου τὸν λόγον καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσω τὸ ὄνομά μου.
3:8.targetText: I know your deeds. See, I have placed before you an open door, which no one can shut. For you have only a little strength, yet you have kept My word and have not denied My name.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The resumptive αὐτήν ("it") repeats the relative which and is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds only for emphasis; the Greek has no word for it.

3:9.sourceText: ἰδοὺ διδῶ ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς τοῦ Σατανᾶ, τῶν λεγόντων ἑαυτοὺς Ἰουδαίους εἶναι, καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν ἀλλὰ ψεύδονται· ἰδοὺ ποιήσω αὐτοὺς ἵνα ἥξουσιν καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιον τῶν ποδῶν σου, καὶ γνῶσιν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἠγάπησά σε.
3:9.targetText: Look at those who belong to the synagogue of Satan, who claim to be Jews but are liars instead. I will make them come and bow down at your feet, and they will know that I love you.

groups.note: BSB renders ἰδού ("behold") as Look at, taking the people named next as its object.
The partitive ἐκ ("some from") is rendered those who belong to.
ψεύδονται ("they lie") is rendered are liars.
The aorist ἠγάπησα ("I loved") is rendered love.

unmappedSource.reason: The broken-off διδῶ ("I give") is taken up again by ποιήσω, and BSB renders the thought once with I will make.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The reflexive ἑαυτούς ("themselves"), subject of the infinitive, is not separately expressed.
BSB leaves καὶ οὐκ εἰσίν ("and they are not") implicit in but are liars instead.
BSB does not render this second ἰδού ("behold").
BSB renders the ἵνα clause after make with a bare infinitive, so ἵνα ("that") is not separately expressed.

3:10.sourceText: ὅτι ἐτήρησας τὸν λόγον τῆς ὑπομονῆς μου, κἀγώ σε τηρήσω ἐκ τῆς ὥρας τοῦ πειρασμοῦ τῆς μελλούσης ἔρχεσθαι ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκουμένης ὅλης, πειράσαι τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
3:10.targetText: Because you have kept My command to persevere, I will also keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.

groups.note: τὸν λόγον τῆς ὑπομονῆς μου ("the word of My endurance") is rendered My command to persevere.
κἀγώ ("and I", "I also") is rendered I … also.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:11.sourceText: ἔρχομαι ταχύ· κράτει ὃ ἔχεις, ἵνα μηδεὶς λάβῃ τὸν στέφανόν σου.
3:11.targetText: I am coming soon. Hold fast to what you have, so that no one will take your crown.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:12.sourceText: Ὁ νικῶν, ποιήσω αὐτὸν στῦλον ἐν τῷ ναῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ μου, καὶ ἔξω οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃ ἔτι, καὶ γράψω ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ μου καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς πόλεως τοῦ Θεοῦ μου, τῆς καινῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἡ καταβαίνουσα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ μου, καὶ τὸ ὄνομά μου τὸ καινόν.
3:12.targetText: The one who overcomes I will make a pillar in the temple of My God, and he will never again leave it. Upon him I will write the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God (the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from My God), and My new name.

groups.note: ἔξω … ἐξέλθῃ ("go out outside") is rendered leave.
The nominative ἡ καταβαίνουσα stands loosely in apposition to Jerusalem; BSB renders it that comes down.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive αὐτόν ("him") is not separately expressed; BSB makes The one who overcomes the object of make.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here, so this καί is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of leave (the temple); the Greek has none.

3:13.sourceText: Ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ Πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.
3:13.targetText: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

3:14.sourceText: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Λαοδικίᾳ ἐκκλησίας γράψον Τάδε λέγει ὁ Ἀμήν, ὁ μάρτυς ὁ πιστὸς καὶ ἀληθινός, ἡ ἀρχὴ τῆς κτίσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ
3:14.targetText: To the angel of the church in Laodicea write:  These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the Originator of God’s creation.

groups.note: The dative ἀγγέλῳ ("to the angel") supplies To.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
Τάδε ("these things") introduces the words that follow.
λέγει ("says") is rendered as the noun phrase the words of.
ἀρχή ("beginning, origin") is rendered Originator.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links this letter to the previous one and is not separately expressed.
The article repeated with πιστός is not separately expressed; BSB uses one the for the faithful and true Witness.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the formula These are the words of; the Greek has none.

3:15.sourceText: Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα, ὅτι οὔτε ψυχρὸς εἶ οὔτε ζεστός. ὄφελον ψυχρὸς ἦς ἢ ζεστός.
3:15.targetText: I know your deeds; you are neither cold nor hot. How I wish you were one or the other!

groups.note: The particle ὄφελον ("would that") is rendered How I wish.
BSB renders ψυχρὸς … ἢ ζεστός ("cold … or hot") here as one or the other.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders this explanatory ὅτι ("that") with a semicolon.

3:16.sourceText: οὕτως, ὅτι χλιαρὸς εἶ, καὶ οὔτε ζεστὸς οὔτε ψυχρός, μέλλω σε ἐμέσαι ἐκ τοῦ στόματός μου.
3:16.targetText: So because you are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold—I am about to vomit you out of My mouth!

unmappedSource.reason: BSB sets neither hot nor cold off with dashes, so this καί is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:17.sourceText: ὅτι λέγεις ὅτι Πλούσιός εἰμι καὶ πεπλούτηκα καὶ οὐδὲν χρείαν ἔχω, καὶ οὐκ οἶδας ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ ταλαίπωρος καὶ ἐλεεινὸς καὶ πτωχὸς καὶ τυφλὸς καὶ γυμνός,
3:17.targetText: You say, ‘I am rich; I have grown wealthy and need nothing.’ But you do not realize that you are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked.

groups.note: χρείαν ἔχω ("I have need") is rendered need.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves this ὅτι ("because"), which leads into the counsel of verse 18, unexpressed.
This ὅτι introduces the quoted words and is not separately expressed.
BSB joins I am rich and I have grown wealthy with a semicolon, so this καί is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB lists these words with commas, so these καί are not separately expressed.

3:18.sourceText: συμβουλεύω σοι ἀγοράσαι παρ’ ἐμοῦ χρυσίον πεπυρωμένον ἐκ πυρὸς ἵνα πλουτήσῃς, καὶ ἱμάτια λευκὰ ἵνα περιβάλῃ καὶ μὴ φανερωθῇ ἡ αἰσχύνη τῆς γυμνότητός σου, καὶ κολλούριον ἐγχρῖσαι τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου ἵνα βλέπῃς.
3:18.targetText: I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined by fire so that you may become rich, white garments so that you may be clothed and your shameful nakedness not exposed, and salve to anoint your eyes so that you may see.

groups.note: ἡ αἰσχύνη τῆς γυμνότητος ("the shame of the nakedness") is rendered shameful nakedness.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists white garments after a comma, so this καί is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:19.sourceText: ἐγὼ ὅσους ἐὰν φιλῶ ἐλέγχω καὶ παιδεύω· ζήλευε οὖν καὶ μετανόησον.
3:19.targetText: Those I love, I rebuke and discipline. Therefore be earnest and repent.

groups.note: The emphatic ἐγώ is the subject of ἐλέγχω ("I rebuke").
ὅσους ἐάν ("as many as") is rendered Those.

3:20.sourceText: Ἰδοὺ ἕστηκα ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν καὶ κρούω· ἐάν τις ἀκούσῃ τῆς φωνῆς μου καὶ ἀνοίξῃ τὴν θύραν, εἰσελεύσομαι πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ δειπνήσω μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς μετ’ ἐμοῦ.
3:20.targetText: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτόν ("to him") unexpressed after come in.

3:21.sourceText: Ὁ νικῶν δώσω αὐτῷ καθίσαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ μου, ὡς κἀγὼ ἐνίκησα καὶ ἐκάθισα μετὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ αὐτοῦ.
3:21.targetText: To the one who overcomes, I will grant the right to sit with Me on My throne, just as I overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.

groups.note: The resumptive αὐτῷ ("to him") gives the To of To the one who overcomes.
κἀγώ ("I also") is rendered I.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object the right for δώσω with an infinitive ("I will give to sit"); the Greek has no noun.

3:22.sourceText: Ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ Πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.
3:22.targetText: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”
